name: Fewster: bound (3) remains valid for g in the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R)

published_statement: 1208.5399 p.10: 'In the m = 0 case, the bound simplifies, and actually gives a bound valid for all m >= 0: INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT_{-oo}^{oo} |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' ... 'The bound requires a certain degree of smoothness in g. In four-dimensions, it remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R), i.e., g, g' and g'' are required to exist (in the distributional sense) and be square-integrable.' p.11: 'But the bound does not apply to g with lower regularity, in particular, to discontinuous g. By sharp switching, one can trap arbitrarily large negative energy densities.' Bound (1), of which (3) is the m-independent weakening, is stated 'for any smooth compactly supported g, and all Hadamard states w' (p.10). The remark is asserted, not proved, in the lecture notes; its rigorous backing is Fewster-Teo gr-qc/9908073 Thm 3.2 (form domain W^{2,2}_0(I), C0^oo(I) a form core; footnote 7: the zero-extension map W^{m,2}_0(I) -> W^{m,2}(R) is a continuous isometry).
published_hypotheses: free real scalar (Klein-Gordon) field, mass m >= 0, minimal coupling (p.10, 27)
4-dimensional Minkowski spacetime ('In four-dimensions', p.10), inertial worldline (t,x) (p.27)
the state w is Hadamard (p.10, footnote 6); the LHS is an expectation value <T00>_w, normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum (p.27)
g real-valued as written g(t)^2 in (3) (the derivation, p.24-25, is for real g, extended to complex g by real/imaginary parts)
base statement: g smooth and compactly supported (p.10, for (1); Theorem 2.4 p.25: g in C0^oo(R)); remark extends to g in W^{2,2}(R), with NO support qualification printed

rederivation.outcome: 29 PASS, 0 FAIL (exit 0; log rederive/run.log). (A, sympy) the clamped mode g = cosh - cos - sigma(sinh - sin): g(0) = g'(0) = g(1) = 0 identically and g'(1)(sinh mu - sin mu)/mu = 2(cos mu cosh mu - 1) identically, so the exact mode is clamped iff cos mu cosh mu = 1; g''(0) = 2 mu^2 != 0; f = g^2 has derivatives 0..3 vanishing at the ends and f''''(0) = 24 mu^4, so f^ ~ u^-5. (B) the zero extension G has weak second derivative g''chi_[0,1] (residual 9e-50 against a smooth test function nonvanishing at 0, 1; CONTROL mu = 4.8 leaves a boundary delta, residual 0.82); sup|g''| = 2 mu^2; G is in W^{2,2}(R) but not W^{3,2} -- it is precisely a non-smooth sampler, the case the remark exists for. (C) Rayleigh quotient = mu_1^4 to 1e-40; C = 3.169858 rounds to Fewster's 3.17. (D) Fourier side: (1/16pi^3) INT_0^oo |G^|^2 u^4 du = (1/16pi^2) INT |g''|^2 to 1.1e-7 relative, integrand tail ~ (g''(0)^2 + g''(1)^2)/u^2 matched; CONTROL box function: RHS partial integral grows as U^3 (ratio 8.01 on doubling), reproducing 'does not apply to discontinuous g' (and FE98 Eq. 6.1). (E) density: C0^oo mollifications g_eps -> G in W^{2,2}; Rayleigh(g_eps) -> mu^4 with deficit/eps = 915.8 +- 0.3% (linear, from the g'' jumps), each above the clamped floor mu^4/(1+2eps)^4 of its longer support; LHS INT rho g_eps^2 -> INT rho G^2 (rel < 1e-4 at eps = 1e-3) for a smooth bounded rho; so (3), true for every C0^oo g, passes to the compactly supported W^{2,2} limit (both sides continuous under W^{2,2} convergence with fixed compact support, since W^{2,2} embeds in C^1 uniformly). Approximants inside C0^oo((0,1)) itself have Rayleigh quotients 608.6, 535.9, 511.2, 504.3 decreasing to mu^4 = 500.56 from above: the infimum in Fewster's p.11 argument is mu^4 and is NOT attained in C0^oo, so Eq. (4) needs only density, whereas the tree's use of the minimiser G itself as the sampler (noise.py:172-174, and the K_F variance at noise.py:1000-1008) is exactly what needs the W^{2,2} remark. (F) the tree's boundary residual scales with working precision (3e-29 at dps 30, 9e-50 at dps 50).

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Teo, gr-qc/9908073, Phys. Rev. D 61 (2000) 084012 ('Quantum inequalities and quantum interest as eigenvalue problems') -- the notes' ref. [36]
later_literature.what: Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 3.1: for rho in their class W_m (which contains every smooth bounded Hadamard energy density), the QI form sum on I has form domain W^{m,2}_0(I) with C0^oo(I) a form core, so QI-compatibility tested on C0^oo(I) is equivalent to positivity on all of W^{2,2}_0(I) (m = 2, 4D). Footnote 7: zero extension W^{m,2}_0(I) -> W^{m,2}(R) is a continuous isometry. This is the rigorous version of the remark for compactly supported g, and it is where the clamped boundary conditions come from (notes' footnote 7). Footnote 11 records that Ford-Roman's delta-pulse sampling function has a square root NOT in W^{2,2}(R) and so is not a legitimate sampler -- the regularity threshold is load-bearing in the literature too. (Earlier than 1208.5399, but it is the source's own backing.)

later_literature.what: Origin of (1)/(3), Eq. (5.5): derived formally ('somewhat formal and lacking in mathematical rigour', Sec. VI) for smooth, even, non-negative sampling functions f of rapid decay, with the state class 'sufficiently well-behaved' left open; Sec. VI speculates smoothness 'could be relaxed to C^k' and shows the box function gives a divergent RHS. It does NOT itself prove the W^{2,2} extension; that rests on Fewster 2000 (gr-qc/9910060, Theorem 2.4 of the notes) plus density/Fewster-Teo. Narrows only the provenance, not the tree's use.

NARROWED also if a sampler used under H4 has g or g' discontinuous at the support edge (a non-clamped mode, e.g. mu not a root of cos mu cosh mu = 1, rederive control B2), since then G'' carries a delta and G is not in W^{2,2}.
